method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse reconstruction of the free-occurrence recursion for all four formula forms, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The removal of assignment dependence for sentences, the free/bound variable distinction, and the inductive definition of free occurrences.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Satisfaction for formulas uses a variable assignment, but sentences should not. A quantifier binds its variable throughout its scope; variables without matching quantifiers are free, and sentences are formulas with no free variables.
samples.checks: The assignment problem, quantifier/variable relation, scope, bound/unbound contrast and proposed sentence definition are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Free occurrences are defined inductively: every occurrence is free in an atomic formula; negation preserves corresponding free occurrences; conjunction takes those free in either side; and an existential binds its own variable while preserving free occurrences of distinct variables from its body.
samples.checks: All four constructor cases, the P(x) example, both biconditionals and the x/y distinction are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A sentence is any formula without a free occurrence of a variable.
samples.checks: The final definition retains both occurrence-level and formula-level conditions.

source_observations: The target consistently uses आस्थिति for a syntactic occurrence and keeps it distinct from the variable itself.
The existential case preserves the difference between binding x and leaving occurrences of a distinct variable x free under an existential on y.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
This introductory recursion omits the additional connectives and universal quantifier handled in the full syntax chapter.
The ordinary Marathi व्याप्ती is used for quantifier scope; exact specialist preference remains open to expert review.
